title: Hoard: from scattered folders to shared resources

scenes.heading: YOUR RESOURCES. ONE PLACE TO FIND THEM.
scenes.caption: Start with the folders you already have. Hoard keeps your files where they are.
scenes.narration: Meet Hoard. Find and share the resources you already have, without moving or renaming your files.

scenes.heading: 01 / SET UP YOUR NODE
scenes.caption: Name this node and review its sharing address. Saved node settings apply after restart.
scenes.narration: Name your node and review its sharing address. Saved settings apply after a restart. This demonstration uses a local address, reachable only from this machine.

scenes.heading: 02 / ADD WHAT YOU ALREADY HAVE
scenes.caption: Choose a folder on the server. Auto-detect works for Git projects, model folders and Hub caches.
scenes.narration: Add a folder from the machine running Hoard. Auto-detect recognizes Git projects, model folders, and Hugging Face caches.

scenes.heading: INDEX IN PLACE
scenes.caption: Add and scan. Sources shows the folder and its scan state; the original files stay untouched.
scenes.narration: Choose Add and Scan. Hoard indexes your resources in place, while your original files stay untouched.

scenes.heading: BRING YOUR COLLECTION TOGETHER
scenes.caption: Add another folder. These tiny synthetic models demonstrate the same flow as a real collection.
scenes.narration: Add another folder to bring your collection together. These small demonstration models show the same workflow you can use with your own collection.

scenes.heading: 03 / FIND YOUR NEXT RESOURCE
scenes.caption: Projects and models share one Index. Select a row for facts; open it when you want more.
scenes.narration: Projects and models share one searchable index. Select a row to see its details in the inspector. Open it when you want to explore further.

scenes.heading: SEARCH THE CONTENT
scenes.caption: Search names, committed README text and file paths. A repository needs no model files to be found.
scenes.narration: Find a project by its name, the text in its read me, or its file paths. A Git project does not need to contain a model.

scenes.heading: REVIEW BEFORE YOU ACQUIRE
scenes.caption: Read the committed README, follow its documentation links and check the selected revision.
scenes.narration: Read the project's documentation before downloading it. Follow links to related guides, and check the selected revision.

scenes.heading: LOOK INSIDE
scenes.caption: Browse files and preview text. Escape returns to the list without losing your place.
scenes.narration: Browse the files and preview their content. Press Escape to return to the file list without losing your place.

scenes.heading: ACQUIRE WITH THE TOOLS YOU KNOW
scenes.caption: Copy the clone command. This walkthrough verifies a real HTTP Git clone and its commit.
scenes.narration: Copy the clone command and use Git as usual. Hoard serves the repository directly, so its source files and documentation travel together.

scenes.heading: FIND IT HERE. SHARE IT FROM HERE.
scenes.caption: For other machines, configure a reachable LAN address. Add more folders whenever you need them.
scenes.narration: To share with other machines, configure a reachable network address and check that it works from another computer. Keep adding folders as your collection grows. Find it, review it, and share it with Hoard.
